title: Choosing Between Triggers, Events, Procedures, and Application Logic knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Choosing Between Triggers, Events, Procedures, and Application Logic”?
options: It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

Server-side SQL objects centralize reusable logic, but their execution context, definer/invoker privileges, side effects, and error paths must be understood. Use the simplest abstraction that keeps behavior testable.
questions.answer_key: Server-side SQL objects centralize reusable logic, but their execution context, definer/invoker privileges, side effects, and error paths must be understood. Use the simplest abstraction that keeps behavior testable.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Server-side SQL objects centralize reusable logic, but their execution context, definer/invoker privileges, side effects, and error paths must be understood. Use the simplest abstraction that keeps behavior testable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Choosing Between Triggers, Events, Procedures, and Application Logic” safely?
options: Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
questions.answer_key: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Choosing Between Triggers, Events, Procedures, and Application Logic”, what should be verified?
options: Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation. The CodeLeaf editor displays reference output only; real behavior depends on the selected server/runtime.
